subject: Reservation structuring & warmup schedule — MosaicThera
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@mosaicthera.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mosaicthera.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Reservation proposal (three-path) + warmup schedule

Hi Amit / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a short proposal that lays out three reservation structures we typically use for customers who want a predictable unit cost while preserving ramp flexibility. Quick highlights inside the PDF but summary below: 

Options (all monthly reserved GPU capacity):
- Pilot Lane: 10 dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA-A100 equivalence), 3-month term, designed for controlled evaluation and prefix cache warmup. Includes 100k warmup token credit.
- Growth Lane: 30 dedicated GPUs, 12-month term, staged ramp (10 → 20 → 30 GPUs across three months), 200k warmup tokens, optional burst pool at 2x baseline for 8 hours/day.
- Production Lane: 80 dedicated GPUs, 12–24 month term, min-guarantee 60 GPUs first 90 days then 80 thereafter, includes 500k warmup tokens and SLA-backed latency tiers.

Key pieces we can customize for MosaicThera based on your traffic profile: minimum active GPUs, phased activation windows, warmup credit cadence, and burst carve-outs for model retrain / large batch jobs. Pricing rows are in the attached PDF and the traffic profile workbook includes our suggested sequencing for KV cache warmup to reduce per-token cost during ramp.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share an internal preference on the three options (Pilot/Growth/Production).
2) We align on min-GPU floor for month 1–3 and any milestone-based ramp triggers (e.g., 50k inference/day triggers +10 GPUs).
3) Procurement reviews terms — we can send a redline-friendly term summary and an activation SOW.

Attachments: 20280329_MosaicThera_Reservation_Options.pdf, mosaic_traffic_profile_q1-q3.xlsx

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@mosaicthera.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mosaicthera.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation proposal (three-path) + warmup schedule

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Alyssa and I reviewed the PDF. A few follow-ups from procurement / engineering: 

- Minimum floor: 10 GPUs for a pilot is fine, but a 30→60 jump for Growth/Production is steeper than we expected. Can you share scenarios where we could start Growth at 20 GPUs (rather than 30) but keep burst headroom?
- Warmup: the token credits are helpful — can warmup credits be spread across the first 2 billing cycles instead of front-loading month 1? That helps our cost forecasts.
- Burst pool: we need guarantees around burst preemption — how long can we expect burst capacity during a scheduled retrain? Also interested in an auto-fallback to a slightly smaller model if capacity constraints occur.
- Procurement: they want a shorter termination window for the first 6 months or a trial exit clause tied to clearly defined performance milestones.

If you can reply with an updated Growth lane starting at 20 GPUs and a proposed ramp tied to concrete triggers + a suggested short trial exit clause, we can push this internally and loop in ProcureOps.

On a separate note: we’d love a short runbook for handling production hot patches if we go to Production lane — who is the on-call, what are escalation SLAs?

—Amit

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reservation proposal (three-path) + warmup schedule — negotiation asks from MosaicThera

Team — forwarding MosaicThera's follow-ups. Highlights: they want Growth to start at 20 GPUs, warmup tokens amortized over two months, clearer burst guarantees and a trial exit clause for first 6 months. They also asked about runbook/on-call for production.

My suggested concessions we can offer without materially changing unit economics:
- Accept Growth start at 20 GPUs for months 1–2, then step to 30 GPUs month 3 if traffic milestones hit. Require an explicit traffic trigger: 40k inference/day sustained over 7 days → +10 GPUs.
- Warmup credit re-schedule: split 200k tokens into 120k month 1 / 80k month 2.
- Burst pool: we can commit to a best-effort burst of up to 2x baseline for scheduled windows (pre-agreed maintenance & retrain windows). For unscheduled spikes, fallback policy is automated routing to a compatible quantized model variant (no SLA guarantee for burst).
- Trial exit clause: allow a 45-day exit within the first 90 days with a pro-rated restocking fee equal to 25% of remaining reserved value — this preserves economics but addresses their risk ask.
- Runbook: stephanie_nguyen in CS maintains the incident runbook; we can include a short appendix in the SOW describing on-call contacts and typical RTO/RPO for different incident severities.

Requesting: marissa — can you confirm approval to offer the 20→30 step with the milestone trigger and the 45-day early exit with 25% restocking bite? karthik — any concerns from an ops capacity perspective if we mark 20 GPUs as the initial minimum but commit to burst best-effort and automatic model fallback?

If we have go-ahead, I'll send a revised PDF and a redlineable term sheet to Amit.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@mosaicthera.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@mosaicthera.com>, procureops@mosaicthera.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation proposal (three-path) + warmup schedule — updated offer

Amit / Alyssa — thanks for the clarity and the quick turnaround from your side. Per our internal alignment, here's the updated Growth lane offer and commercial guardrails we can put in the SOW: 

Updated Growth lane (custom for MosaicThera):
- Initial reservation: 20 dedicated GPUs (month 1–2).
- Phased ramp: month 3 → 30 GPUs conditional on traffic trigger: sustained 40k inference/day for 7 days.
- Warmup credits: 200k tokens split across month 1 (120k) and month 2 (80k).
- Burst pool: scheduled burst windows up to 2x baseline for pre-agreed retrain windows (we will list weekly retrain slots in the SOW). Unscheduled burst is best-effort; automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model variant will be enabled to preserve latency.
- Trial exit: 45-day early termination window available within the first 90 days; early-exit fee = 25% of remaining reserved contract value to cover fleet rebalancing and capacity commitments.

Operational addenda we will include in the SOW:
- Incident runbook appendix (contacts, on-call rotations) — CS will provide a three-page runbook.
- Escalation SLA for P1 incidents: initial response 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 2 hours; full postmortem within 5 business days.
- Capacity fallback: automatic routing to quantized model variant with transparent logging to your console.

If this looks good, I'll: (1) attach an updated PDF with redline-friendly clauses, (2) send a short SOW appendix for procurement to review, and (3) schedule a 30-minute call with our CS lead to walk through the runbook.

Would you like us to include a small pilot discount for months 1–2 if you sign before Apr 15? We can consider a 10% concession on reserved GPU unit price for the initial two months.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
